title: Vali's questioning Rama's propriety
introduction: Rama's arrow hits Vali on chest and Vali fallen down. But Vali is not dead yet. When Rama and Lakshmana approach dying Vali, he questions the propriety of Rama in killing him. Vali's questioning explicitly is straightforward befitting to the defeated mighty Vanara King. But implicitly, there are ancient commentaries that deduce many more meanings in picturising Vali as a devotee of Rama, who wanted to die at the hand of Rama, like Viraadha and others, as a means of salvation.
closing: 1 - parāñmukha vadham kṛtvā ko atra prāptaḥ tvayā guṇaḥ; 2 - daṇḍayaḥ ca api apakāriṣu; 3 - na mām anye sañrabdham pramattam veddum arhasi; 4 - viṣaye vā pure na apakāromi;l 5 - hiñsya akilbiṣam; 6 - phala mūla aśina nityam; 7- bhūmiḥ hiraṇyam rūpyam ca vigrahe kāraṇāni na; 8 - tvam tu kama pradhānaḥ ca; 9 - hatvā mām iha kim vakṣyasi satām madhye; 10 coraḥ prāṇi vadhe rataḥ ādi niraya gāminaḥ; 11 - adhāryam carmam abhakṣyāṇi ca māñsāni; 12 pañca pañca nakā a bhakṣyāḥ; 13 maithilīm aham ca ānītavān bhave; -- dharmākūtam

1] By killing one who is facing away, what worth is achieved by you?; 2] You have not punished the wrongdoer; 3] Killed one who is combating with another and an unvigilant one; 4] In your country or city I did no misdeed; 5] Non-guilty being is hurt; 6] Fruits, tuber eating being is killed; 7] No dispute of land, gold or silver; 8] You primary aspiration is to kill without probing into good or bad; 9] How do you face criticism by scholars?; 10] Unnecessary killers are hell-goers; 11] Un-wearable is my skin uneatable is my flesh; 12] Five kinds of five-nailed animals are usable by humans; 13] I would have brought back Maithili in one day.
For all these questions Rama answers in next chapter and speaks as to how justified is this elimination, to Vali and to all of us.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे सप्तदशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 17th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ततः शरेण अभिहतो रामेण रण कर्कशः |
पपात सहसा वाली निकृत्तैव पादपः
verses.iast:
tataḥ śareṇa abhihato rāmeṇa raṇa karkaśaḥ |
papāta sahasā vālī nikṛttaiva pādapaḥ
verses.translation: When Rama's arrow hit him then Vali, the scourger in war, suddenly fell down like a hewed down tree.

glosses.meaning: by Rama , by his arrow, completely hit

verses.devanagari:
स भूमौ न्यस्त सर्वांगः तप्त कांचन भूषणः |
अपतत् देव राजस्य मुक्त रश्मिर् इव ध्वजः
verses.iast:
sa bhūmau nyasta sarvāṃgaḥ tapta kāṃcana bhūṣaṇaḥ |
apatat deva rājasya muk{}ta raśmir iva dhvajaḥ
verses.translation: He who glittered with pure golden ornaments, that Vali fell down on earth while all of his limbs sank to dust, like the flag of Indra when released from its ropes.

glosses.meaning: one with melted, golden, ornaments [who glittered]
he, on earth [into dust,] kept [sank,] all, body-parts

verses.devanagari:
अस्मिन् निपतिते भूमौ हरि ऋषाणाम् गणेश्वरे |
नष्ट चन्द्रम् इव व्योम न व्यराजत मेदिनी
verses.iast:
asmin nipatite bhūmau hari ṛṣāṇām gaṇeśvare |
naṣṭa candram iva vyoma na vyarājata medinī
verses.translation: On the fall of that lord of hosts of monkeys and bears onto earth, unilluminated is the earth like the welkin that has forsooth lost its moon.

glosses.meaning: for monkeys, for bears, hosts of, lord's
on his, on earth, when fell

verses.devanagari:
भूमौ निपतितस्य अपि तस्य देहम् महात्मनः |
न श्रीर् जहाति न प्राणा न तेजो न पराक्रमः
verses.iast:
bhūmau nipatitasya api tasya deham mahātmanaḥ |
na śrīr jahāti na prāṇā na tejo na parākramaḥ
verses.translation: Though that great souled Vali fell onto earth, neither his brilliance, nor lives, nor resplendence, nor his bravery are unfettering from his body.

glosses.meaning: of great-soul one, his, from body

verses.devanagari:
शक्र दत्ता वरा माला कान्चनी रत्न भूषिता |
दधार हरि मुख्यस्य प्राणान् तेजः श्रियम् च सा
verses.iast:
śakra dattā varā mālā kāncanī ratna bhūṣitā |
dadhāra hari mukhyasya prāṇān tejaḥ śriyam ca sā
verses.translation: That superb and gem-studded golden pendent given by Indra sustained that monkey chief's lives, resplendence and brilliance.

verses.devanagari:
स तया मालया वीरो हैमया हरियूथपः |
संध्यानुगत पर्यन्तः पयोधर इव अभवत्
verses.iast:
sa tayā mālayā vīro haimayā hariyūthapaḥ |
sandhyānugata paryantaḥ payodhara iva abhavat
verses.translation: By still wearing that golden chest-pendant around his neck, that brave general of monkeys Vali appeared like a black-cloud smeared with the colour of golden sunset all around its edges.

glosses.meaning: brave one, he that Vali, monkeys, general of
golden one, by that [by wearing it,] pendant
colour of sunset, traced with - smeared with
water, bearing [black-cloud,] like, he became [appeared to be.]

verses.devanagari:
तस्य माला च देहः च मर्मघाती च यः शरः |
त्रिधा इव रचिता लक्ष्मीः पतितस्य अपि शोभते
verses.iast:
tasya mālā ca dehaḥ ca marmaghātī ca yaḥ śaraḥ |
tridhā iva racitā lakṣmīḥ patitasya api śobhate
verses.translation: Even though Vali has fallen on ground his splendour is as though refulgent devising itself into three aspects, namely by his body, chest-pendant, and the arrow of Rama, which arrow is given to strike the crucial body parts alone, and which is still stuck in Vali's chest.

glosses.meaning: crucial-organ [heart in chest,] striking, which, arrow is
in three ways, written [crafted, devising,] splendour, as though

verses.devanagari:
तत् अस्त्रम् तस्य वीरस्य स्वर्ग मार्ग प्रभावनम् |
राम बाणासन क्षिप्तम् आवहत् परमाम् गतिम्
verses.iast:
tat astram tasya vīrasya svarga mārga prabhāvanam |
rāma bāṇāsana kṣiptam āvahat paramām gatim
verses.translation: That arrow which effectuates the pathway to heaven, now discharged from the bow of Rama has brought forth that redemption to brave Vali .

verses.devanagari:
तम् तथा पतितम् संख्ये गत अर्चिषम् इव अनलम् |
ययातिम् इव पुण्यान्ते देव लोकात् परिच्युतम्
आदित्यम् इव कालेन युगान्ते भुवि पातितम् |
महेन्द्रम् इव दुर्धर्षम् उपेन्द्रम् इव दुस्सहम्
महेन्द्र पुत्रम् पतितम् वालिनम् हेम मालिनम् |
व्यूढ उरस्कम् महाबाहुम् दीप्तास्यम् हरि लोचनम्
लक्ष्मण अनुचरो रामो ददर्श उपससर्प च |
verses.iast:
tam tathā patitam saṅkhye gata arciṣam iva analam |
yayātim iva puṇyānte deva lokāt paricyutam
ādityam iva kālena yugānte bhuvi pātitam |
mahendram iva durdharṣam upendram iva dussaham
mahendra putram patitam vālinam hema mālinam |
vyūḍha uraskam mahābāhum dīptāsyam hari locanam
lakṣmaṇa anucaro rāmo dadarśa upasasarpa ca |
verses.translation: Then on seeing him who has fallen in war, the one with golden pendant, enormously chested, mightily armed, face golden, eye greenish, but who is like a fire extinct of its flame; who is like Indra in unassailability and like Upendra in indomitability; and who like Yayaati who has fallen from heaven, as well like the sun who falls onto earth from solar orbit when Time-ender flings him at the end of era; such as he is, on seeing that son of Indra, who forsooth has fallen, Rama neared him followed by Lakshmana.
notes: Yayaati is the son of Nahusha, who was a king of repute. After a rigorous penance Yayaati attains heaven. But he starts his self-praise and goes on narrating his achievements. Indra tries to tell him that 'this is heaven, here there is no you-ness and I-ness...' but in vain. Later unable to contend with Yayaati's self-eulogy Indra pushes him back to mortal worlds. Vali is in the same predicament as he took pride in his own brawny strength but now battered by still mightier person.

glosses.meaning: at era, end, on earth, flung

verses.devanagari:
तम् तथा पतितम् वीरम् गत अर्चिष्मतम् इव अनलम्
बहुमान्य च तम् वीरम् वीक्षमाणम् शनैरिव |
उपयातौ महावीर्यौ भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
verses.iast:
tam tathā patitam vīram gata arciṣmatam iva analam
bahumānya ca tam vīram vīkśamāṇam śanairiva |
upayātau mahāvīryau bhrātarau rāma lakśmaṇau
verses.translation: On seeing the brave Vali fallen like that, who by now is like fire with extinguished tongues of flames, and who is seeing droopily, those two valiant brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, neared him with due honour.

glosses.meaning: extinguished, tongues of flame, fire, like
slowly - droopily, thus, who is seeing

verses.devanagari:
तम् दृष्ट्वा राघवम् वाली लक्ष्मणम् च महाबलम् |
अब्रवीत् परुषम् वाक्यम् प्रश्रितम् धर्म संहितम्
स भूमौ अल्पतेजोसुः निहतो नष्ट चेतनः |
अर्थ सहितया वाचा गर्वितम् रण गर्वितम्
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā rāghavam vālī lakṣmaṇam ca mahābalam |
abravīt paruṣam vākyam praśritam dharma saṃhitam
sa bhūmau alpatejosuḥ nihato naṣṭa cetanaḥ |
artha sahitayā vācā garvitam raṇa garvitam
verses.translation: On seeing Rama and the great mighty Lakshmana as well, he who fell to ground flatly hurt by arrow, and whose energy and lives are trifling and vigour trivialised thereby, that Vali spoke these sarcastic words in his proper pride to Rama, who is taking pride in this conflict as a victor, which words at the same time have meaning, politeness, and self-righteousness.

glosses.meaning: who is on earth [fallen to earth]
[to Rama who in this] conflict, taking pride [of victory]
meaning, containing, with words - with meaningful words

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रथितः प्रिय दर्शनः |
पराङ्मुख वधम् कृत्वा को अत्र प्राप्तः त्वया गुणः |
यदहम् युद्ध सम्रब्धः त्वत् कृते निधनम् गतः
verses.iast:
tvam narādhipateḥ putraḥ prathitaḥ priya darśanaḥ |
parāñmukha vadham kṛtvā ko atra prāptaḥ tvayā guṇaḥ |
yadaham yuddha sam.hrabdhaḥ tvat kṛte nidhanam gataḥ
verses.translation: "You are a renowned prince with pleasing looks.. but, which kind of death I am getting now, that too when I was in the commotion of conflict with another, alas, that ignoble death is owing to you, and what merit is achieved by you in this undertaking of yours to kill someone who is facing away from you...
notes: From hereon the sentences of Vali and also of Rama in next chapter are commented variously and voluminously. Apart from upholding Rama's deed as a rightful one, Vali's position is also kept up, by deducing meaning from these utterances and Vali is pictured as a dedicate to the Absolute. Maheshvara Tiirtha in his Ramayana tattva diipika gives many tones for these aspects, mainly as innuendo of praise, vyāja ninda.

In this verse itself Vali's expression is said to be like this: parāñmukha vadham kṛtvā = 'one who is faced way - not in battlefield, but in the battle field like life, say from morality and doing all unethical things, like exiling younger brother and captivating his wife... killing of such an antagonist is rightful of you...' For another compound kaḥ atra prāptaḥ tvayā guṇaḥ other mms use kaḥ nu prāptaḥ tvayā guṇaḥ in that nu has a special usage in Ramayana, as at 1-1-2 konvasmin sāmpratam loke etc. Here also, taking kaḥ nu guṇaḥ it is said that 'verily invaluable merit is achieved by you and your godhood is established by absolving me. For me, getting killed at your hand is no less a merit, by which I am rid of all sins, and I am now going to heavens...' This is supported by scriptures rājatva śāśan pāpasyatadāpnoti kilbiṣam 'one who is rightfully punished by the king is rid of all sins'; and according to the saying as well: rāja bhidhṛta daṇḍāstu kṛtvā pāpāni mānavāḥ | nirmalaḥ svargam āyānti santa sukṛto yathā and I will go to heavens without blemish'.

For the last compound tvat kṛte nidhanam gataḥ other mms use śareṇa urasi tāditaḥ 'with arrow, on chest, struck...' establishing that Rama did not backstab Vali, but hit on chest as said at 4-16-35: vāli vakṣasi pātitaḥ.

glosses.meaning: conflict, one who is in commotion of
by you, done - owing to you
which [kind of death, ignoble death,] demise, I went - I got death
one facing away [from you,] killing him, on undertaking

verses.devanagari:
कुलीनः सत्त्व संपन्नः तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः |
रामः करुणवेदी च प्रजानाम् च हितेरतः
सानुक्रोशो महोत्साहः समयज्ञो दृढव्रतः |
इति एतत् सर्व भूतानि कथयन्ति यशो भुवि
verses.iast:
kulīnaḥ sattva sampannaḥ tejasvī caritavrataḥ |
rāmaḥ karuṇavedī ca prajānām ca hiterataḥ
sānukrośo mahotsāhaḥ samayajño dṛḍhavrataḥ |
iti etat sarva bhūtāni kathayanti yaśo bhuvi
verses.translation: "Rama is high-born, they say, gifted with mightiness, resplendent, pursuer of vows, mindful of mercy, delighter in people's welfare, sympathetic, greatly enthusiastic and assertively committed in doing good deeds, knower of time-and-action, all these living-beings on earth are thus relating your renown, aren't they.
notes: Explicitly it is Vali's harsh accusation of Rama, but implicitly it is a praise offered to Rama, since his arrow accords heavens to Vali. This is the same with the following two verses. vyāja ninda innuendo of praise.

glosses.meaning: time, knower of - knower of timely action
all, living beings, on earth, are relating.

verses.devanagari:
दमः शमः क्षमा धर्मो धृति सत्यम् पराक्रमः |
पर्थिवानाम् गुणा राजन् दण्डः च अपकारिषु
verses.iast:
damaḥ śamaḥ kśamā dharmo dhṛti satyam parākramaḥ |
parthivānām guṇā rājan daṇḍaḥ ca apakāriṣu
verses.translation: "To be able to control senses and will, forgiveness, conscientiousness, resoluteness, truthfulness, and adventurousness, oh, king, are the aptitudes of a king, and even punishing the wrongdoers, too.

verses.devanagari:
तान् गुणान् संप्रधार्य अहम् अग्र्यम् च अभिजनम् तव |
तारया प्रतिषिद्धो अपि सुग्रीवेण समागतः
verses.iast:
tān guṇān sampradhārya aham agryam ca abhijanam tava |
tārayā pratiṣiddho api sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ
verses.translation: "Concluding that those kingly characteristics will be obtainable in you, and even judging by the noble dynasty of yours, I have confronted Sugreeva though Tara dissuaded me.

glosses.meaning: those, [kingly] characteristics [will be obtainable in you]
of your, noble, dynasty, also [judging by your dynasty]

verses.devanagari:
न माम् अन्येन संरब्धम् प्रमत्तम् वेद्धुम् अर्हसि |
इति मे बुद्धिर् उत्पन्ना बभूव अदर्शने तव
verses.iast:
na mām anyena saṃrabdham pramattam veddhum arhasi |
iti me buddhir utpannā babhūva adarśane tava
verses.translation: "When you have not appeared before me when I confronted Sugreeva my concept was, 'it will be inapt of Rama to hurt me while I am combating with another combatant, besides, when I will be unvigilant in that fight...'

glosses.meaning: to wound [to hurt,] [how] not, apt of him
thus, my, concept, came up, became.

verses.devanagari:
न त्वाम् विनिहत आत्मानम् धर्म ध्वजम् अधार्मिकम् |
जाने पाप समाचारम् तृणैः कूपम् इव आवृतम्
verses.iast:
na tvām vinihata ātmānam dharma dhvajam adhārmikam |
jāne pāpa samācāram tṛṇaiḥ kūpam iva āvṛtam
verses.translation: "Not known that your soul is put to death, not known that you are the unrighteous flag bearer of righteousness, to me not known that you are insidious like straw covered well.
notes: In the verse the two words na, jāne 'not known to me' are used only once. While bringing it two more times for filling the ellipses, adhyāhāra, meaning is drawn to all three expressions as above i.e., 'Unknown are the three things... etc.' Vali is said to have admitted that Supreme Soul is not a struck-out entity or killable, and either sin or profanity is attachable to Him, as per the saying in Bhagavad Gita, kam ghātayati hanti kam? 'who can stab the soul, who hurts it... na enam cindanti śasrāṇi 'knife can cleave It not...' as at 2-21 and its successive verses. Here Vali has said that 'nobody knows, including me... that you are flag-bearer of virtue above individual souls, sins...'

glosses.meaning: completely, down, trodden, minded - one who killed one's own soul]

verses.devanagari:
सताम् वेष धरम् पापम् प्रच्छन्नम् इव पावकम् |
न अहम् त्वाम् अभिजानामि धर्म छद्माभि संवृतम्
verses.iast:
satām veṣa dharam pāpam pracchannam iva pāvakam |
na aham tvām abhijānāmi dharma chadmābhi saṃvṛtam
verses.translation: "I have no knowledge that you are a sinner, one in the garb of a benign soul, and explicitly mantled under the garb of probity like ash covered fire.
notes: The word pāpam is either sin or sinner. If it is said as sin, then it is attached to next compound then it is read as the admission of Vali in noticing Rama as Supreme Person, pāpam pracchannam iva pāvakam , 'as fire will burn the one who is covered with sin, you also will burn...' And there is no 'garb of dharma...' to you, for you are dharma itself. Thus Vali said to have noticed Supreme in Rama, as said at apahata pāpmatvādi guṇa viśiṣṭa 'Supreme Person is one who is above the words like sins, merits' etc.

verses.devanagari:
विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा पापम् करोमि अहम् |
न च त्वाम् अवजाने अहं कस्मात् त्वम् हंसि अकिल्बिषम्
फल मूल अशनम् नित्यम् वानरम् वन गोचरम् |
माम् इह अप्रतियुध्यन्तम् अन्येन च समागतम्
verses.iast:
viṣaye vā pure vā te yadā pāpam karomi aham |
na ca tvām avajāne ahaṃ kasmāt tvam haṃsi akilbiṣam
phala mūla aśanam nityam vānaram vana gocaram |
mām iha apratiyudhyantam anyena ca samāgatam
verses.translation: "I am non-guilty as I have not committed any misdeed either in your country or in your city, nor I have taunted you; I am a vanara subsisting on fruits and tubers and always moving in forests alone; such as I am, what made you to torture me when I was not combating with you en face, furthermore, when I was involved with another?
notes: 'You do not kill any guiltless beings, tvam api a+kilbiṣam na himsi , but you are now killing me because there is some guilt in my deeds, of which I am well aware, but waited for you to come...' This is the subtext of Vali's retrospection.

glosses.meaning: I your, country, or, city, or
not, countering [you, not en face] while combating

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रतीतः प्रियदर्शनः |
लिन्गम् अपि अस्ति ते राजन् दृश्यते धर्म सम्हितम्
verses.iast:
tvam narādhipateḥ putraḥ pratītaḥ priyadarśanaḥ |
lingam api asti te rājan dṛśyate dharma samhitam
verses.translation: "You are renowned to be a prince with charming looks, oh, king, and indications agreeable to rectitude are also appearing on your body.

glosses.meaning: you are, pleasing, in your looks

verses.devanagari:
कः क्षत्रिय कुलेजातः श्रुतवान् नष्टसंशयः |
धर्म लिंग प्रतिच्छन्नः क्रूरम् कर्म समाचरेत्
verses.iast:
kaḥ kṣatriya kulejātaḥ śrutavān naṣṭasaṃśayaḥ |
dharma liṃga praticchannaḥ krūram karma samācaret
verses.translation: "Will anybody born in Kshatriya's family, a learned one in Veda-s, thereby who is rid of ambiguities with respect to right and wrong, and who is cloaked in an air of probity, execute such a ruthless deed like this?

glosses.meaning: in Kshatriya, family, one born in
rid of, ambiguities [of right and wrong]
ruthless, deed [like this one, killing me,] executes.

verses.devanagari:
राम राघव कुले जातो धर्मवान् इति विश्रुतः |
अभव्यो भव्य रूपेण किम् अर्थम् परिधावसे
verses.iast:
rāma rāghava kule jāto dharmavān iti viśrutaḥ |
abhavyo bhavya rūpeṇa kim artham paridhāvase
verses.translation: "Though born in Raghava's dynasty and renowned as a moralist you are actually amoral, and for what purpose you run around with this moral aspect?
notes: 'Oh, Rama, you took birth, not so, emerged as an incarnation in Raghava's dynasty, artham purposefully... abhavya san 'though cruel...' bhavya rūpeṇa paridhāvasi, kim? you are moving about with a superficial aspect of a morally sagacious person, or what? No definitely. krūra karma samācaret? or did you do a wrongdoing in killing me? Not so.

If it is said that you are an incarnate on earth, there cannot be duality in your inner aspect or outer aspect. You cannot have a cruel heart with a charming face of a prince, when you alone are the protector of Universe. Equally, taking birth in Raghava-s lineage you cannot move about with a sagely appearance and go on killing beings like me. So, there shall be some purpose in killing me. artham kim 'what is that purpose...'

This is Vali's self-assurance that Rama is the Supreme Being, but killed him with some purpose, and he would like to know that purpose. In this sequence, Vali assumes that Rama killed him in his search for Seetha, and thus Vali tells Rama 'if that is the only reason I would have brought Seetha in one day without any bloodshed…' The purpose for Vali's elimination is nothing but the elimination of Ravana.

glosses.meaning: for what, purpose, you run after - run around.

verses.devanagari:
साम दानम् क्षमा धर्मः सत्यम् धृति पराक्रमौ |
पार्थिवानाम् गुणा राजन् दण्डः च अपि अपकारिषु
verses.iast:
sāma dānam kṣamā dharmaḥ satyam dhṛti parākramau |
pārthivānām guṇā rājan daṇḍaḥ ca api apakāriṣu
verses.translation: "Influencing, largesse, forbearance, probity, candour, and conquering are the attributes of the kings, oh, king, and even punishing the wrongdoers.
notes: 'The first said political strategies sāma, dāna, bheda, may not work with me because I am not a coequal of yours in kingship, so the last one, daṇda, 'punishing the wrongdoer,' is enough to eliminate me, for I must have committed wrongs.'

verses.devanagari:
वयम् वनचरा राम मृगा मूल फल अशनाः |
एषा प्रकृतिर् अस्माकम् पुरुषः त्वम् नरेश्वरः
verses.iast:
vayam vanacarā rāma mṛgā mūla phala aśanāḥ |
eṣā prakṛtir asmākam puruṣaḥ tvam nareśvaraḥ
verses.translation: "We as animals live in forests while you are city dwellers, we live by eating fruits and tubers while you enjoy feasts and banquets, our nature is such to kill and get killed, thus you and me have no correlation. And you, even if you are a man and a prince for humans, you resorted to this animalistic way of killing me lying in the wait, thus your action is worse than that of an animal, if not subhuman or un-princely.
notes: The stress of Vali is on his animality. Being a man why killing a monkey unworthy in rituals or in diet, is his question. [cf. 38 and 39 verses of this chapter.] Are they just monkeys - is the subsequent question. If these Vanara-s were to be a just fruit-eating animals why Vali used to offer sandhya , time-oriented oblations to gods as stipulated in Veda-s, in an unusual way of swinging from one ocean to the other. And why Tara, who is said to be the knowers of Vedic hymns, as in previous chapter bid svastyayanam , bon voyage with Vedic hymns to Vali? This is because of the superiority of vanara race than animals.

The other argument of Vali is like this: 'We are animals living in forests and unlike elephants, horses and the like, we are not even fit to render service to mankind, doing which those animals enjoy high grade foods than us, while we are destined to eat fruits and tubers. When there is no rapport between you humans and we monkeys, and then there can be no enmity between you and me, because enmity crops up only when there is a correlation. Apart from this, I am no equal of yours, but inferior and worthless vanara, and hence your killing me is only to give me salvation.' Maheshvara Tiirtha.

glosses.meaning: you are, human's, king, a man

verses.devanagari:
भूमिर् हिरण्यम् रूपम् च निग्रहे कारणानि च |
तत्र कः ते वने लोभो मदीयेषु फलेषु वा
verses.iast:
bhūmir hiraṇyam rūpam ca nigrahe kāraṇāni ca |
tatra kaḥ te vane lobho madīyeṣu phaleṣu vā
verses.translation: "Territory, gold, and silver will be the causes while counteracting somebody, in that case, by what you are decoyed into these forests of mine or in the fruits of mine.
notes: The statements of 'my forests... my fruits...' will be retorted by Rama in the next chapter.

verses.devanagari:
नयः च विनयः च उभौ निग्रह अनुग्रहौ अपि |
राज वृत्तिर् असंकीर्णा न नृपाः काम वृत्तयः
verses.iast:
nayaḥ ca vinayaḥ ca ubhau nigraha anugrahau api |
rāja vṛttir asaṅkīrṇā na nṛpāḥ kāma vṛttayaḥ
verses.translation: "In the pairs of propriety and compliance, punishment and pardoning, no admixture is exercised in kingcraft, for the kings do not conduct themselves volitionally.
notes: Vali's statement is: 'Even the ordinary rulers on earth do not conduct themselves without adhering to their codes of conduct, then what is there to speak of you who is the Ruler of Universe. So, you must have imposed this punishment without mixing the pairs of opposites that results in my salvation...'

glosses.meaning: in propriety, also, in compliance, also
kings, volitionally, conduct themselves, they do not.

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् तु काम प्रधानः च कोपनः च अनवस्थितः |
राज वृत्तेषु संकीर्णः शरासन परायणः
verses.iast:
tvam tu kāma pradhānaḥ ca kopanaḥ ca anavasthitaḥ |
rāja vṛtteṣu saṅkīrṇaḥ śarāsana parāyaṇaḥ
verses.translation: "But, to you your self-interests are primary, and you are a wrathful, capricious, contriver of kingcraft, and an impetuous shooting-happy archer.

glosses.meaning: [achievement of your own] desire, is primary to you [self-interested]
in king's, duties, concocting - contriver of kingcraft
arrow, seating [on the taut of bowstring,] engaged in, [shooting-happy archer.]

verses.devanagari:
न ते अस्ति अपचितिः धर्मे न अर्थे बुद्धिर् अवस्थिता |
इन्द्रियैः काम वृत्तः सन् कृष्यसे मनुजेश्वर
verses.iast:
na te asti apacitiḥ dharme na arthe buddhir avasthitā |
indriyaiḥ kāma vṛttaḥ san kṛṣyase manujeśvara
verses.translation: "Oh, king, you have no devotion to probity, nor your mind is firm about material gains, but as a free-willed one you are distracted by senses.
notes: "The 'Lord of People' is the Supreme Person incarnated himself as a king of humans as per the derivation of the word nārāyaṇa , one who conducts humans to and fro from him. tvam 'you...' ; Here the tu is as in verse at 4-17-33, i.e., kim ardhaka, kim Are you? ; So, tvam kāma pradhānaḥ 'you are the primary one to humans to aspire for. While all the created beings aspire one thing or the other, humans have many more wants. But above all these human wants, you are the primary-want to be desired or aspired for salvation.' avāpta samasta kāmanaḥ 'you do not have any aspiration or desire for yourself...' kopanaḥ ' in punishing the wrongdoers you are a wrathful one...' anavasthitaḥ 'unstable, ever-moving, dynamic in maintaining universe. ' rāja vṛttaiḥ ca samkīrṇaḥ is read otherwise as rāja vṛtteṣu samkīrṇaḥ 'concocted is your kingly orientation, for you wear cloths like a saint and yet handle weaponry, whereas in actuality there no garb for you.' The first compound in 4-17-34 is read as te dharme apacitiḥ na 'you have no sincerity in ordinary scripture-laid virtues...' and then it is said, 'scriptures and canons are for ordinary humans but you are above them... so you are beyond the ordinary canons that emerged for humans' kāma vṛtte san ' you are independent in your deeds or movements...' indriyaiḥ kṛṣyase, kim? 'are you drawn away by senses, or what? No. You cannot be drawn away by the horses called senses for you are the holder of their reins. So you are the jana īśvara Supreme Lord for the people, as king of people, or as the Supreme Person who took incarnation as Rama.

glosses.meaning: [your] intellect, in material gains, not, firm
by wishes, operating [free willed,] as you are

verses.devanagari:
हत्वा बाणेन काकुत्स्थ माम् इह अनपराधिनम् |
किम् वक्ष्यसि सताम् मध्ये कर्म कृत्वा जुगुप्सितम्
verses.iast:
hatvā bāṇena kākutstha mām iha anaparādhinam |
kim vakṣyasi satām madhye karma kṛtvā jugupsitam
verses.translation: "How you are answerable to gentlemen, Rama, when you have done this detestable deed of killing an unoffending one like me with your arrow?
notes: Since this killing of Vali is an intricate act, some may point out that Rama is at fault in killing Vali. But Vali states here inversely that, "you may inform gentlemen who may point out that this act of yours in killing me is a wrongdoing... you may say them that 'I have killed a wrongdoer so I am not at fault...' " Vali has no need to say repeatedly that he is killed by the arrow of Rama, as he is not killed by a sword or cudgel. But, it is to be repeated necessarily to remind that the arrow came from an unknown destination.

glosses.meaning: me, now, by arrow, on killing
gentlemen, amongst, what, you will tell - how you are answerable.

verses.devanagari:
राजहा ब्रह्महा गोघ्नः चोरः प्राणिवधे रतः |
नास्तिकः परिवेत्ता च सर्वे निरय गामिनः
verses.iast:
rājahā brahmahā goghnaḥ coraḥ prāṇivadhe rataḥ |
nāstikaḥ parivettā ca sarve niraya gāminaḥ
verses.translation: "A regicide, a Brahman-cide, a cow-slayer, a thief, an inveterate killer, an atheist, and an younger brother who marries before his elder, all of them will go to hell.

glosses.meaning: beings, in killing, one engaged in - an inveterate killer
who marries before the marriage of his elder brother

verses.devanagari:
सूचकः च कदर्यः च मित्र्घ्नो गुरुतल्पगः |
लोकं पापात्मानम् एते गच्छन्ते न अत्र संशयः
verses.iast:
sūcakaḥ ca kadaryaḥ ca mitrghno gurutalpagaḥ |
lokaṃ pāpātmānam ete gacchante na atra saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "A slander-monger, skinflint, friend-killer and one who makes love with his teacher's wife, they all go to the worlds of evil-souls, no doubt about it.

glosses.meaning: with teacher's, bed, enterer [ love-maker with teacher's wife]
of evil, souled ones, to worlds, they go

verses.devanagari:
अधार्यम् चर्म मे सद्भी रोमाणि अस्थि च वर्जितम् |
अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि त्वत् विधैः धर्मचारिभिः
verses.iast:
adhāryam carma me sadbhī romāṇi asthi ca varjitam |
abhakṣyāṇi ca māṃsāni tvat vidhaiḥ dharmacāribhiḥ
verses.translation: "My skin is unwearable, holy people forbid my hair and bones, and uneatable is my meat for your kind of reputable people.
notes: Tiger's skin is used as carpet, its two canine teeth are used in golden necklaces, its other body parts are said to contain medicinal properties, and hence the numbers of tigers are dwindling, especially in India. Elephant's tusks are great decorative articles. Camel's bones are made into bangles and bracelets. Rhino's horn has religious use as well as a decorative article. Caamara, Himalayan-yak's hair is used for royal fanning instruments. Deerskin has its own place in high religious seats of saints and sages. Hence the poachers are making a fortune on this fauna. But the skin, bones, or hair of monkey, or to that matter of fact any item of a monkey is not of any use either in religious or in medicinal or for decorative purposes. Hence, they are not killed for food, game or poaching.

glosses.meaning: your, kind of, by virtue, pursuers - reputable people

verses.devanagari:
पंच पंच नखा भक्ष्या ब्रह्म क्षत्रेण राघव |
शल्यकः श्वाविधो गोधा शशः कूर्मः च पंचमः
verses.iast:
paṃca paṃca nakhā bhakṣyā brahma kṣatreṇa rāghava |
śalyakaḥ śvāvidho godhā śaśaḥ kūrmaḥ ca paṃcamaḥ
verses.translation: "Raghava, five kinds of five-nailed animals, viz., a kind of wild rodent, a kind of wild-boar, a kind of lizard, a hare and fifthly the turtle are edible for Brahmans and Kshatriya-s.

glosses.meaning: a kind of boar that kills dogs, wolves etc

verses.devanagari:
चर्म च अस्थि च मे राजन् न स्पृशन्ति मनीषिणः |
अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि सो अहम् पंच नखो हतः
verses.iast:
carma ca asthi ca me rājan na spṛśanti manīṣiṇaḥ |
abhakṣyāṇi ca māṃsāni so aham paṃca nakho hataḥ
verses.translation: "Sensible people will not touch my skin and bones, oh, king, nor meats from my body are to be eaten, such as I am, a five-nailed animal, I am killed.
notes: 'There appears to be no reason as to why a five-nailed animal like me is to be killed, when there is no reason for political, religious, hunting, or food purposes. Then this act of yours shall have an ultimate purpose isn't it....'

glosses.meaning: meats, also a bhakSyaaNi = not, to be eaten
such as I am, I am killed.

verses.devanagari:
तारया वाक्यम् उक्तो अहम् सत्यम् सर्वज्ञया हितम् |
तद् अतिक्रम्य मोहेन कालस्य वशम् आगतः
verses.iast:
tārayā vākyam uk{}to aham satyam sarvajñayā hitam |
tad atikramya mohena kālasya vaśam āgataḥ
verses.translation: "Though Tara appraised me with truthful and favourable words, I just disregarded her advise owing to my own delusion, and gone into the control of Time.
notes: Though dissuaded by Tara, kālasya vaśam āgataḥ, satyam; I am bound to come here for my time is over and I am destined to die at the hands of the Supreme Being. Or, to say clearly īśvarasya vaśam āgataḥ, satyam 'I have come under the control Supreme, truly...' where kālaḥ, Time, is another name for Supreme Being; kālo asmi loka kśaya kṛt pravaddhaḥ... kala

glosses.meaning: I am, truthful, favourable, words, said - appraised
under Time's, control, I have gone in.

verses.devanagari:
त्वया नाथेन काकुत्स्थ न सनाथा वसुंधरा |
प्रमदा शील संपूर्णा पति एव च विधर्मिणा
verses.iast:
tvayā nāthena kākutstha na sanāthā vasundharā |
pramadā śīla sampūrṇā pati eva ca vidharmiṇā
verses.translation: "With you as her espouser the Earth is not with a correct spouse, as with any lady who is with full-fledged chastity, but with a husband who is without rectitude.
notes: The king is usually the lord of land. Vishnu is the husband of Earth, bhū devi. Here Rama is both. Here Vali's contention is, 'unlike a husband without rectitude, you will safeguard the land truthfully as you have all the attributes of a lord of land and a good husband. duṣṭa nigrahatvādi kalyāṇa guṇa rūpeṇa. So, you will protect Earth by eradicating evildoers on it... like me...'

glosses.meaning: earth, by husband, by you - you as her husband
with chastity, endowed, lady - as with

verses.devanagari:
शठो नैकृतिकः क्षुद्रो मिथ्या प्रश्रित मानसः |
कथम् दशरथेन त्वम् जातः पापो महात्मना
verses.iast:
śaṭho naikṛtikaḥ kṣudro mithyā praśrita mānasaḥ |
katham daśarathena tvam jātaḥ pāpo mahātmanā
verses.translation: "How are you borne to that great-souled Dasharatha when you are artful, felonious, knavish, disposed to a false modesty subconsciously, and an evildoer?
notes: 'You are born to great-souled Dasharatha, yato mahātmanā daśarathena jātaḥ... katham śaṭhaḥ? 'being the son of such a great-soul Dasharatha, how can you be artful, felonious?

glosses.meaning: you are, by great-souled, Dasharatha, given birth.

verses.devanagari:
छिन्न चारित्र्य कक्ष्येण सताम् धर्म अतिवर्तिना |
त्यक्त धर्म अंकुशेन अहम् निहतो राम हस्तिना
verses.iast:
chinna cāritrya kakṣyeṇa satām dharma ativartinā |
tyak{}ta dharma aṃkuśena aham nihato rāma hastinā
verses.translation: "I am killed by an elephant called Rama that snapped off its girdle-cord called tradition, that infringed the conventions of righteous people, and that discarded the goad called virtue.
notes: The girdle-cords, called vāri in Sanskrit foot-cords or girdle cords. The goads of rulebooks etc., are required to the humanly elephants that move in herds, break their cords of traditions, cultures and social values. The Supreme Being is not so, as said later by himself naiva tasya kR^te na artho in Bhagavad Gita at 3-18 and also at saṅkarsaya ca kartāa syām 3-24. 'So getting eliminated from this mortality by no less than the Supreme Being is my fortune.'

glosses.meaning: righteous people's, conventions, over, stepping - infringed

verses.devanagari:
अशुभम् च अपि अयुक्तम् च सताम् च एव विगर्हितम् |
वक्ष्यसे च ईदृशम् कृत्वा सद्भिः सह समागतः
verses.iast:
aśubham ca api ayuk{}tam ca satām ca eva vigarhitam |
vakśyase ca īdṛśam kṛtvā sadbhiḥ saha samāgataḥ
verses.translation: "On accomplishing this sort of unpropitious, unjustified killing, which is condemned by the righteous people, what can you say when you meet the godly men?
notes: Vali is saying in vyāja ninda praise in innuendo. Taking the last word Vali is prompting Rama to say like this: samāgataḥ is cleaved as saḥ māgataḥ, mām gataḥ 'he, that Vali, Me, reached...' Vali attained salvation and reached Me. a+śubham ca a+yuktam ca api san, mām gataḥ 'Though Vali's actions are unpropitious, unjustified and condemnable by the righteous, but by Me eliminated he attained Me, the Supreme Being...' And this agrees with mṛtyuḥ sarva haraḥ ca aham Gita - 10-34 'I am the death, an all- exhausting-one.'

glosses.meaning: by righteous people, also, thus, condemned
this sort of deed - killing, on accomplishing

verses.devanagari:
उदासीनेषु यो अस्मासु विक्रमो अयम् प्रकाशितः |
अपकारिषु ते राम न एवम् पश्यामि विक्रमम्
verses.iast:
udāsīneṣu yo asmāsu vikramo ayam prakāśitaḥ |
apakāriṣu te rāma na evam paśyāmi vikramam
verses.translation: "The valour that which is displayed on the unprejudiced few like us, oh, Rama, I do not see that sort of valour is shown by you in respect of your enemies.
notes: The word vikrama is triumphing, and treading as well. Taking the meaning of Rama's treading up to Vali it is said as below. apakāriṣu 'perpetrating evil on your dedicates like Sugreeva, Hanuma et al' ; asmāsu 'on us, myself, Tara, and Angada' te your yaḥ 'those feet, that are impossible to be seen by Brahma and others; vi krama valour / treading; pradarśitaḥ udāsīnesu that are displayed, to great-souls and saints; na paśyāmi hitherto I have not seen.

You have shown mercy on us namely myself, Tara, Angada and other adherents of mine, though we have perpetrated evil in respect of your adherents like Sugreeva, Hanuma et al. You have shown mercy by way of your treading towards me on your divine feet, which feet will not be revealed even to Brahma, but at times you reveal them to sages and saints. I have seen them now. Had I seen these Divine Feet earlier, I would have suddenly fallen on them long back, like Sugreeva. But, I do not foresee advancement of the same feet towards the real wrongdoers, namely Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Indrajit, as yet.

glosses.meaning: unprejudiced ones, in respect of us
which, this kind of, valour, shown
in respect of your, evil doers [enemies like Ravana]

verses.devanagari:
दृश्यमानः तु युध्येथा मया युधि नृपात्मज |
अद्य वैवस्वतम् देवम् पश्येः त्वम् निहतो मया
verses.iast:
dṛśyamānaḥ tu yudhyethā mayā yudhi nṛpātmaja |
adya vaivasvatam devam paśyeḥ tvam nihato mayā
verses.translation: "Had you been in combat with me en face oh, prince, you would have been killed by me and by now you would have seen the death-god Yama.
notes: Rama might have cut a sorry face for he did not confront Vali vis-à-vis on field, but shot his arrow from afar. Vali says for this, 'it is impossible for others to confront me... but to you nothing is impossible... and you might have confronted me.' Here the word yadi is used in sense kim arthaka i.e., 'or what?' adya mayā dṛśyamānā san, yuddhyethā api 'today even if you fight with me manifestly, that too before me... mayā hataḥ san, vaivasvata devam paśeḥ, kim? 'by me killed though, do you see Yama, Death-god, or what?

'It is impossible for others to confront me in combat, and for you there is nothing called impossibility. Other way round, though you confront me in person can I fight you back? Can I kill an unkillable entity? Thinking that, though I am capable of killing you, and hopefully kill you, do you wish to see a lesser god like Yama in naraka the Hell. Improbable and impossible are all these suppositions, and thus this act of eliminating me cannot be called a killing, but 'according salvation' by you the Supreme, in person.'

glosses.meaning: in war, while you are being seen - confronting me
with me, if you have combated
by now, you, Yama, god, would have seen.

verses.devanagari:
त्वया अदृश्येन तु रणे निहतो अहम् दुरासदः |
प्रसुप्तः पन्नगेन इव नरः पाप वशम् गतः
verses.iast:
tvayā adṛśyena tu raṇe nihato aham durāsadaḥ |
prasuptaḥ pannagena iva naraḥ pāpa vaśam gataḥ
verses.translation: "An unassailable one, such as I am, I am killed by you while you remained invisible on the field of fight, as with a sinner bitten by a snake while he is asleep.
notes: Vali is said to be lamenting to have lost his chance to confront Rama face to face in fight. The word pāpavaśam gato aham is read as pāna vaśam gato aham in other mms. Meaning that 'a drunken man bitten by snake' and this drunkenness is attributed to Vali and said as:
'In my own drunkenness of unassailable might, I could not see and confront you in fight, and had I been sober, though dead at your hands, I would have been victorious in going to heavens...'

Secondly, it is not Rama that has not shown himself up, it is Vali who did not try to find where Rama is. Rama is aware of the boon given by Brahma to Vali āhūya vālinam brahmā dadau varam anuttamam | pratīpavarti nobhūyāt artha balam arindama || Summoning Vali, Brahma gave an unexcelling boon... any combatant confronting Vali will loose half of his strength to Vali... Knowing this through Sugreeva, and honouring Brahma's boon Rama did not come face to face with Vali. This is said at 4-16-27, and 4-16-31. The same is the situation when Hanuma is bound by Brahma missile in Sundara Kanda, where he obliges Brahma's decree.
āhūya vālinam brahmā dadau varam anuttamam | pratīpavarti nobhūyāt artha balam arindama ||

Knowing this through Sugreeva, and honouring Brahma's boon Rama did not come face to face with Vali. This is said at 4-16-27, and 4-16-31. The same is the situation when Hanuma is bound by Brahma missile in Sundara Kanda, where he obliges Brahma's decree.

glosses.meaning: unassailable one, that is what I am
in fight, un, seen - invisible one, by you

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीव प्रिय कामेन यद् अहम् निहतः त्वया |
माम् एव यदि पूर्वम् त्वम् एतद् अर्थम् अचोदयः |
मैथिलिम् अहम् एक आह्ना तव च आनीतवान् भवेः
राक्षसम् च दुरात्मानाम् तव भार्य अपहारिणम् |
कण्ठे बद्ध्वा प्रदद्याम् ते अनिहतम् रावणम् रणे
verses.iast:
sugrīva priya kāmena yad aham nihataḥ tvayā |
mām eva yadi pūrvam tvam etad artham acodayaḥ |
maithilim aham eka āhnā tava ca ānītavān bhaveḥ
rākśasam ca durātmānām tava bhārya apahāriṇam |
kaṇṭhe baddhvā pradadyām te anihatam rāvaṇam raṇe
verses.translation: "For which purpose I am killed, intending to do good to Sugreeva is incidental to it, you should have assigned me for that purpose in the first instance itself, and I would have brought that evil-minded demon Ravana, the abductor of your wife in one day, that too without killing him in any fight, but by fastening him by neck, and I would have presented Maithili to you.
notes: Rama's approaching Vali for help is an impossible thing. Rama has come all along searching for Sugreeva and befriended him. Also given is the word to Sugreeva to kill Vali. Rama's going back on his own word can never happen. puts it as:
abhaye vāline datte pratijña parihīyate | rāvaṇasya sakhā vālī rāvaṇo api vrajettu mām | rāvaṇasya vadha abhāvāt avatāra phalam na hi |

If Vali is excused, promise given to Sugreeva fails. Ravana is Vali's friend and even Ravana may come running to Rama seeking refuge, and then leaving Ravana without killing, leaves no fruits of incarnation. Vali's logic is that Ravana alone is the evil minded one in abducting Seetha. How about his own action in incarcerating Ruma, Sugreeva's wife? If this is asked Vali might have replied to save his face, 'I am an animal and those adductions, seductions etc., do not work in our animal kingdom, and we enjoy what we want.' But it is not so with Veda practising Vanara-s. Hence this race is given the title of Vanara, neither animal, nor monkey, nor human.

glosses.meaning: Sugreeva, good, intending to do, only
earlier, me, only, should have prayed, if - if you have assigned me alone, earlier
Maithili, also, is brought, she would have been.

verses.devanagari:
न्यस्ताम् सागर तोये वा पाताले वा अपि मैथिलीम् |
आनयेयम् तव आदेशात् श्वेताम् अश्वतरीम् इव
verses.iast:
nyastām sāgara toye vā pātāle vā api maithilīm |
ānayeyam tava ādeśāt śvetām aśvatarīm iva
verses.translation: "I would have brought Maithili at your order even if she is lodged in oceanic waters or in nether worlds, as with the White Horse of Vedic lore.
notes: There is one Upanishad called śveta aśvatara Upanishad and when it was in the shape of white female horse, this horse was stolen by Madhu and Kaitabha demon-brothers and later retrieved by Hayagreeva, another aspect of Vishnu.

verses.devanagari:
युक्तम् यत् प्रप्नुयात् राज्यम् सुग्रीवः स्वर् गते मयि |
अयुक्तम् यद् अधर्मेण त्वया अहम् निहतो रणे
verses.iast:
yuk{}tam yat prapnuyāt rājyam sugrīvaḥ svar gate mayi |
ayuk{}tam yad adharmeṇa tvayā aham nihato raṇe
verses.translation: "The fact of Sugreeva's getting the kingdom after my going to heaven is proper, but the fact of your killing me in war, unrighteously, is improper.
notes: Why Vali banished Sugreeva from kingdom is being explained. a + dharmeṇa ' un-righteously ...'; by the unjust deed of Sugreeva's closing the face of cave when I was fighting with Dundubhi, wishful of my death and thus; sugrīvaḥ rājyam prāpnuyāt iti yat tat a + yuktam ' Sugreeva's getting this kingdom unrighteously, is improper.' aham tvayā raṇe nihataḥ itaḥ param mayi svar gatena ata sugrīvo rājyam rājyam prāpnuyāt iti yat tat yukatam ' on my going to heavens his getting the kingdom is proper.'

'As long as I am alive Sugreeva can never get a chance to rule the kingdom, because he ascended throne improperly and unrighteously when I am alive in the cave. Because he closed the entrance of the cave, wishing me to die therein, when I was still fighting with Dundubhi, I had to banish him. Now that I am going to heaven at your mercy, his getting the throne of Kishkindha at your mercy, and as its one time regent, is proper.'

glosses.meaning: Sugreeva, [kingdom,] will get, thus, that which [fact is]
I am, in war, by you
un, righteously, killed, thus, that which

verses.devanagari:
कामम् एवम् विधम् लोकः कालेन विनियुज्यते |
क्षमम् चेत् भवता प्राप्तम् उत्तरम् साधु चिंत्यताम्
verses.iast:
kāmam evam vidham lokaḥ kālena viniyujyate |
kṣamam cet bhavatā prāptam uttaram sādhu ciṃtyatām
verses.translation: "Admittedly the world is this way, and if possible a relevant reply may gently be thought ofabout your propriety in killing me..." So said Vali to Rama.
notes: For the above the latent meaning of Vali is: lokaḥ ' people, living beings...'; evam vidhaḥ cet ' like me sinners, if they become...'; kāmam kālena viyujyate ' desirably by Time, Yama, people will be disposed'; bhavatā prāptam uttaram 'from you, received, reply - in the shape of killing me; uttamam ' the best'; kśamam ' proper one'; cintyatām 'you shall think that way only';

If people become sinners like me, Time, Yama disposes them off desirably, and the reply for my sins received from you in the shape of your arrow in my chest, is the best and a proper one too, so it shall be thought of, not otherwise."

verses.devanagari:
इति एवम् उक्त्वा परिशुष्क वक्त्रः
शर अभिघातात् व्यथितो महात्मा |
समीक्ष्य रामम् रवि संनिकाशम्
तूष्णीम् बभौ वानर राज सूनुः
verses.iast:
iti evam uk{}tvā pariśuṣka vak{}traḥ
śara abhighātāt vyathito mahātmā |
samīkṣya rāmam ravi saṃnikāśam
tūṣṇīm babhau vānara rāja sūnuḥ
verses.translation: That great-souled son of a vanara king Vali, whom the arrow impaled and agonised, on keenly seeing Rama whose resplendence equals the brightness of the sun, said that much and remained silent when his mouth has dried up.
notes: Rama has not used any great or deadly arrow on Vali, but a third rated or lesser one is shot at, because Vali is still lingering with the same arrow in his chest. The same is said in Yuddha kanda, 67th chapter, 154 verse, where Valmiki himself is amazed to say that Kumbhakarna is not killable with that sort of arrow which pierced through seven great sala trees, and which has killed the greatest Vali. yaiḥ sāyakaiḥ sāla varā nikṛttā, vālī hato vānara puñgavaḥ ca... and narrating thus the poet says that Vali is nothing when compared with Kumbhakarna and others in Lanka.
